subject: Action required: customer-reported p99 spikes for multi-tenant long-context requests
messages:
-----Original Message-----
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@cardioai.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Severe p99 spikes for 16k/32k requests - CardioAI production errors

Hi Priyom,

We started seeing significant p99 spikes and a ~4x increase in timeouts this morning on the hosted API for our long-context job submissions. The failures are affecting inference batches that use 16k and 32k windows (mostly system-messages + transcript).

What we observe:
- p50/p90 unchanged, p95 up ~1.3x, p99 up ~3.8x compared to baseline.
- Errors are timeouts and 502s for jobs that previously completed in ~450ms p99.
- Impact started around 08:30 PT and is sustained.

I've attached a short sample of requests and timestamps (sample-requests.txt) and an error snippet. This is customer-urgent — we are in the middle of a rollout to 10k users and this is blocking.

Can you escalate to engineering and let me know immediate mitigation? We need either a rollback or a config workaround. Also please advise whether this will be covered under SLA credits.

Thanks,
Rachel
VP Engineering, CardioAI


-----Reply from priyom.das@redwood.ai-----
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@cardioai.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe p99 spikes for 16k/32k requests - CardioAI production errors

Thanks Rachel — I’m escalating now and we’ll prioritize triage. Initial ask: can you confirm whether the failing requests are multi-part conversations (system + long transcript) or single-prompt long tokens? Any example request IDs helps.

Action items from our side (immediate):
- SRE to check worker OOMs / queue depth and p99 graphs (Vivek, Soojin)
- Runtime team to check KV cache hit rate and memory pressure for long-context handling (Laura)
- I’ll propose a short mitigation (rate-limit long-context at tenant level or short-term config to force streaming cut) within 2 hours.

We’ll update with a concrete mitigation and ETA.

Best,
Priyom
Account Exec, Redwood Inference


-----Internal: Vivek Kulkarni -> engineering-triage -----
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe p99 spikes for 16k/32k requests - CardioAI production errors

Quick summary of what I'm seeing from the initial logs (attaching p99-graphs.png and logs.zip):
- Around 08:20 PT we started seeing an uptick in queueing on the hosted API. CPU is fine; tail latency correlates with worker-side GC/evictions under heavy KV cache churn.
- Multiple workers serving multi-tenant pools received concurrent 32k attachments; KV cache miss rate jumped ~27% for large prefixes. Missing KV leads to repeated full-attention recompute and KV memory churn.
- In two clusters we saw transient OOMs (OOM killed process, automatic restart). Those restarts created request-in-flight queuing which amplified p99.

Immediate recommendation:
1) Short-term: Apply per-tenant soft rate limit for requests with token_count > 8k to reduce burst; enable request-splitting fallback (split long transcripts into chunked calls) as customer workaround.
2) Medium-term: Apply a hot-cache pinning for stability and increase per-worker KV memory reserve while we finish a better LRU/eviction policy.

I’ll start a canary of the per-tenant soft limit in us-west-2 and monitor p99; expect a measurable drop if queueing is the driver.

-Vivek
Sr. Director, Infra


-----Internal: Soojin Lee -> priyom.das, Laura Bennett, Vivek Kulkarni -----
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe p99 spikes for 16k/32k requests - CardioAI production errors

Triage notes / mitigation plan (short window):
- Deployed tenant-level soft caps: any single request with token_count > 8k will enter a queued path with a controlled concurrency of 3 per-tenant (config key: hosted.max_long_context_concurrency).
- Enabled immediate request-splitting fallback in the runtime for tenants that have long-context flags set. Splitting policy: chunk <= 8k and stitch outputs server-side to preserve conversational state for the caller. This is a temporary shim (mitigation-runbook.pdf attached).
- Started canary in us-west-2 at 10:10 PT. Watching p99, queue depth, and restart counts.

Expected outcome: if KV-miss-induced recompute and process churn are the cause, we should see p99 drop within 30-45 minutes on canary traffic and partial improvement on global traffic as soft caps propagate.

If this reduces customer impact we will:
- Keep soft caps in place for 48 hours, continue hot-fixing eviction policy, then roll a kernel-level memory reserve in 72 hours.
- Open SUP-9876 for follow-up engineering work.

-Soojin
SRE Lead


-----Priyom -> CardioAI (external update)-----
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@cardioai.com>, support@cardioai.com
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe p99 spikes for 16k/32k requests - CardioAI production errors

Rachel — quick update: we’ve rolled a temporary mitigation that should reduce the p99 tail for long-context submissions. Actions taken:
- Activated a soft tenant-level concurrency cap for requests > 8k tokens (limits burstiness).
- Enabled runtime fallback that splits requests > 8k into chunked calls and stitches results server-side (preserves ordering and context).

Request for you: if possible, throttle client-side submissions that exceed 8k tokens for the next 24 hours while we stabilize (this will keep your success rates high). We’ll monitor and share p99 graphs in 1 hour.

We’ve flagged this for SLA credit review; I’ll follow up separately on credits. If you’d like an exec-level call I can set one up with Vivek.

Apologies for the disruption — we’re treating this as priority.

Best,
Priyom
Account Exec, Redwood Inference


-----Final internal summary (Vivek -> leadership)-----
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 May 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-mortem summary: CardioAI p99 regression from long-context workloads

Summary:
- Root cause: Multi-tenant KV cache churn + transient worker OOMs under bursts of 16k/32k requests. High KV miss rate forced repeated full-attention recompute and memory churn, causing process restarts and queuing which amplified p99.
- Impact: CardioAI production p99 increased ~3.8x during peak window on 2028-05-22, affecting ~12% of requests with token_count > 8k.
- Mitigation: tenant soft caps (<=8k soft path) + runtime request-splitting reduced p99 to within 1.2x baseline on canary; global rollout completed within 12 hours.

Next steps (owners & ETA):
1) Runtime: implement improved eviction policy + hot-pin hot prefixes (Laura) — ETA 7 days.
2) Infra: increase per-worker KV reserve and add health-check throttles to avoid churning restarts (Vivek) — ETA 72 hours.
3) CS/Sales: follow up on SLA credits and a customer exec call (Priyom) — ETA 24 hours.

Notes: We should consider adding a product-level knob to set tenant long-context limits with graceful client-facing error messages to avoid surprise failures.

Attachments: p99-graphs.png, logs.zip, mitigation-runbook.pdf

-Vivek
Sr. Director, Infra
